question.text: Under Section 5 of PMLA, the provisional attachment of property suspected to be proceeds of crime can be ordered for a period not exceeding:

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5 of PMLA empowers the Director, or any officer not below the rank of Deputy Director authorised by him, to provisionally attach property suspected to be proceeds of crime for a period not exceeding 180 days from the date of the order. The order must be based on a "reason to believe" recorded in writing. The Trap: 90 days and 120 days are common distractor periods drawn from other financial regulations and compliance timelines. 365 days is far too long for a "provisional" attachment under PMLA. Note: Workbook reference: NISM Series XXIV p.29. The "reason to believe" must be recorded in writing -- this is the key safeguard against arbitrary attachment.
